summary: The upgrade from Ubuntu 22.04 to 24.04 will introduce several changes and potential issues, particularly affecting Apache2, PHP, GCC, init, and SSH configurations.

claims.text: Apache2 in Ubuntu 24.04 supports mod_md configurations via a local tailscale daemon and uses pcre2 (10.x) for regular expression evaluation instead of the deprecated pcre (8.x).
PHP in Ubuntu 24.04 now automatically restarts Apache2 after an upgrade, whereas previously it would only notify the user to manually restart the service.
Ubuntu 24.04 uses systemd v255.4, which introduces several new features and changes in how services are managed.
OpenSSH in Ubuntu 24.04 uses systemd socket activation by default, which may require adjustments to existing configurations.
Ubuntu 24.04 includes known issues that users should be aware of, such as significant bugs and deprecation warnings for certain features.
The default Ubuntu Desktop installation in 24.04 is minimal, with an extended selection option available for additional applications.
